ansibleBecome.description: Allows you to force privilege escalation.

ansibleBecomeExe.description: Allows you to set the executable for the escalation method you selected.

ansibleBecomeFlags.description: Allows you to set the flags passed to the selected escalation method

ansibleBecomeMethod.description: Allows you to set the privilege escalation method to a matching become plugin.

ansibleBecomePassword.description: Allows you to set the privilege escalation password.

ansibleBecomeUser.description: Allows you to set the user you become through privilege escalation.

ansibleConnection.description: Specifies the connection type to the host. This can be the name of any Ansible connection plugin. SSH protocol types are ssh or paramiko. The default is ssh.

ansibleHost.description: Specifies the resolvable name or IP of the host to connect to, if it is different from the alias (name) you wish to give to it.

ansiblePassword.description: The password to use when connecting (logging in) to the host.

ansiblePort.description: The connection port number, if not the default (22 for ssh).

ansiblePrivateKeyFile.description: Private key file used by SSH. This is useful if you use multiple keys and you do not want to use SSH agent.

ansiblePythonInterpreter.description: Allows you to set the Python interpreter to use for the target system.

ansibleSftpExtraArgs.description: Extra arguments to pass to the sftp command.

ansibleShellExecutable.description: Allows you to set the shell executable to use for the target system.

ansibleShellType.description: Specifies the shell type of the target system. You should not use this setting unless you have set the `ansibleShellExecutable` to a non-Bourne (sh) compatible shell. By default, Ansible formats commands using sh-style syntax. If you set this to csh or fish, commands that Ansible executes on target systems follow those shell’s syntax instead.

provider.description:
The provider type for the ansible package. By default, resources use package-wide configuration
settings, however an explicit `Provider` instance may be created and passed during resource
construction to achieve fine-grained programmatic control over provider settings. See the
[documentation](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/reference/programming-model/#providers) for more information.

args.description: Used to build arguments to run Ansible playbook with.

checkMode.description: If 'true', playbook execution won't make any changes but only change predictions will be made.

diffMode.description: If 'true', when changing (small) files and templates, differences in those files will be shown. Recommended usage with 'check_mode'.

extraVars.description: A map of additional variables as: { key-1 = value-1, key-2 = value-2, ... }.

forceHandlers.description: If 'true', run handlers even if a task fails.

groups.description: List of desired groups of hosts on which the playbook will be executed.

ignorePlaybookFailure.description: This parameter is good for testing. Set to 'true' if the desired playbook is meant to fail, but still want the resource to run successfully.

limits.description: List of hosts to include in playbook execution.

name.description: Name of the desired host on which the playbook will be executed.

replayable.description: If 'true', the playbook will be executed on every 'terraform apply' and with that, the resource will be recreated. If 'false', the playbook will be executed only on the first 'terraform apply'. Note, that if set to 'true', when doing 'terraform destroy', it might not show in the destroy output, even though the resource still gets destroyed.

tags.description: List of tags of plays and tasks to run.

tempInventoryFile.description: Path to created temporary inventory file.

vaultPasswordFile.description: Path to a vault password file.

verbosity.description: A verbosity level between 0 and 6. Set ansible 'verbose' parameter, which causes Ansible to print more debug messages. The higher the 'verbosity', the more debug details will be printed.
